editorial.creator: Bandcamp Daily
editorial.lede: Bandcamp Daily published a September 15 scene report mapping current gqom through labels, geography and artists rather than reducing the genre to a playlist.
body: The useful angle is scene structure: who is releasing the music, where activity is concentrated, and how the genre's rhythmic vocabulary is changing after wider international attention.
Read it as a current map of a living scene, not as a definitive history of gqom.

editorial.title: Cloudflare Pages Functions + D1
editorial.lede: The existing Feeds prototype used Cloudflare Pages Functions with D1 bindings as an example of keeping a Vite frontend static while API routes handled durable state.
body: The durable lesson is narrower than the old implementation: D1 migrations are sequential SQL files tracked in the repository, and bindings can expose the database to server-side request handlers.
Phase 1 has since superseded D1 as an editorial content store. This item therefore belongs as a technical explanation of the earlier mechanism, not as the target Feeds architecture.

assertions.text: Pages Functions support bindings, including D1 bindings.
D1 migrations are represented as ordered SQL migration files.

metadata.selectionReason: It preserves a useful technical mechanism from the existing project history while separating that mechanism from the now-superseded editorial-D1 architecture.

editorial.title: Notebook Special 2026
editorial.creator: MUBI Notebook
editorial.lede: MUBI Notebook's 2026 annual special combines festival criticism, archival rereleases, interviews, comics, games and city-level film culture in one editorial package.
body: The table of contents is useful as a map of what film criticism can look like when it behaves like curation rather than review aggregation.
Skim the package first, then choose one strand—an interview, an archive piece, a festival report or another form—and follow that rather than trying to consume the whole issue linearly.
editorial.entryPoint: Start with the table of contents and use it to pick one unfamiliar form of film writing.
